SEARCH
Package chess.service

Class Game

java.lang.Object
chess.service.Game
public class Game extends Object
Runs a game of chess: holds the board and both players, tracks whose turn it is and the move history, checks every move against the rules, and tells its listeners what happened.

Game never reads input or prints output. It returns a MoveResult and notifies GameListeners (the Observer pattern), so the console, the Swing GUI and the logger all work with the same class. The rules themselves live in ChessRules.

All standard rules are implemented, including king safety, castling, en passant, promotion to a chosen piece, checkmate and stalemate. Draws by repetition, the fifty-move rule and insufficient material are not.

  • Method Details

    • start

      public final void start()
      Sets up the starting position, gives White the first move, and clears the winner and move history. Also used to restart a game. It is final because the constructor calls it, so subclasses can't change it.

    • loadPosition

      public void loadPosition(List<Piece> pieces, PieceColor toMove)
      Replaces the board with a custom position, used by the tests to set up stalemate and special moves quickly. The history is cleared.
      Parameters:
      pieces - the pieces to place, each on its own position
      toMove - the side to move first
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if either king is missing

    • resetState

      private void resetState(PieceColor toMove)

      Parameters:
      toMove - the side to move first

    • tryMove

      public MoveResult tryMove(Position from, Position to, PromotionPiece promotion)
      Tries to move the current player's piece from one square to another.

      The move is accepted only if it is in the piece's list of legal moves from ChessRules. If it isn't, the reason is worked out for the message, nothing changes, and listeners are told it was rejected.

      Parameters:
      from - the square of the piece to move
      to - the destination square
      promotion - the piece to promote to if this is a promotion
      Returns:
      a successful result describing the move, or a failure explaining why not
